blocks.content: Article 32 is the very heart and soul of the Constitution, without which this Constitution would be a nullity.

rows: Ensures equality before law, prohibits discrimination, untouchability, and titles.
Guarantees six basic freedoms, protection in respect of conviction, life, personal liberty, and arrest.
Prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and employment of children in hazardous jobs.
Guarantees freedom of conscience, religious practice, propagation, and management of religious affairs.
Protects language, script, and culture of minorities and their right to establish educational institutions.
Provides right to move Supreme Court via writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

items: Rights available ONLY to Citizens: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30.
Fundamental Rights under Articles 20 and 21 CANNOT be suspended even during a National Emergency (Article 359).
The Right to Property was converted from a Fundamental Right to a legal right under Article 300-A by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) deals with Fundamental Rights, often referred to as the Magna Carta of India.
Originally, the Constitution provided for seven Fundamental Rights, but the Right to Property (Article 31) was removed by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
The Right to Property is now a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII of the Constitution.
Fundamental Rights are justiciable in nature, allowing citizens to move directly to the Supreme Court (Article 32) or High Courts (Article 226) for their enforcement.
Rights under Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are available exclusively to Indian citizens, whereas other rights extend to foreigners as well.
